questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to improve my oral english skills and thus wanted to go to a place where people talk enligsh on a daily basis. Given that my aim was to explore new cultures and try different ways of learning, North Carolina seemed like a good place to go to.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got to travel a lot. I gained new academic skills and was so lucky to become close friends with my roomie. On the other hand, I would have preferred to go on an exchange sooner, especially given the High School Musical environment that you experience at NC State. I unfortunately did not have the opportunity to go earlier because of Covid-19.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find the information. The international office at NC State is very helpfull and answers quickly. They held introductory meetings on Zoom where they provided us with relevant information   about what to do before arriving i.e. housing, visa, insurance etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an introductory session where they welcomed us and gave important information. You could always go to them for help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Welcoming and helpfull.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of opportunities including doorms (own bathroom, shared kitchen), residence halls (shared bathroom, no kitchen), and apartments (own bathroom, own kitchen). Most of the exchange students that I talked with lived in the Avent Ferry Complex (doorm), Alexander Hall (residence hall), or Wolf Ridge Apartments (apartments). Alexander Hall is very close to the center of campus. Avent Ferry is a doorm complex with the larges rooms compared to other doorms. It is placed a bit "off campus" compared to Alexander Hall, which is very central, and the same goes for Wolf Ridge Apartments.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There are not many cooking facilities. Americans are known for eating take away or being in a meal plan. You can have different meal plans depending on how much you eat in a day. I was actually surprised that the dining halls were quite good. I however did not have a meal plan so I bought a meal when I went to the dining hall of which there are three (I think). Otherwise I bough take-away or cooked a meal in our shared kitchen at Avent Ferry.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: On-campus housing is expensive but the same goes for off-campus housing. If you choose to find something off-campus you should be carefull, because most of the contracts are for a one-year period and not a semester which means that you have to pay the rent for a year. I wanted housing to be easy and something that I should not worry about, and I therefore chose on-campus housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I mean it is a doorm. It is small and expensive, and nothing to write home about. Also, given that I was only there for a semester, I did not want to buy a lot of stuff to make it cosy to just throw it out again.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy because the staff sort of managed it for you. However, I found it difficult to choose a course because there are so many.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I filled out a file with the courses that I wanted and then they handled it from there. If you wanted to change or drop a course (which is very common) you just told them to help you or deleted them yourself.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I got help from the Poole College of Management on campus.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successfull. I got the classes that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Reach out for help is you are in doubt. They are more than willing to help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was different than home, because of the way that they teach and how they put the final grade together. You have to participate physically, do a bunch of homeworks (almost on a weekly basis) etc. because the final grade is made up by participation, assignments, exam. In some courses, there are no final examination.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two doctoral-courses and one graduate course. The levels of the courses are as follows: 100-400 are undergraduate courses,  500-600 are graduate, and 700-899 are doctoral courses. The level of the courses are lower than the level at UCPH. However, the doctoral classes require a bit more time than the graduate courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There are more class debate, presentations and homeworks compared with UCPH. The courses that I took only had 10-13 people in them so it is a different environment to be in. The style of teaching made it feel more like being back in High School.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECG 590 Special Economic Topics: Health Economics & Policy
ECG 707 Topics in Industrial Organization
ECG 715 Environmental and Resource Economics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
ECG 590 is a good course in the sense that you learn about the US Health Care System and the subjects in this course are relevant and interesting. It is however only descriptive and not theoretical nor empirical with the exception that you learn a bit about natural experiments / quasi-experimental design through reading the research articles. 

ECG 707 is a good course with a passionated lecturer! You learn a lot in this course and the papers are interesting to read. The assignments can be a bit tough but you can get help from the professor if you ever get stuck. However, be prepared to do a lot of empirical tasks in different programs (STATA, Python, Matlab etc.) It is a learning-by-doing course as you are not teached how to code. 

ECG 715 is a heavy theoretical course with no slides and in my opinion they teached us in some of the more boring subjects within the field. I would not recommend this course.

questions.answer: Vaccination costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than I thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were so many clubs. I signed up for the sailing club which was a lot of fun.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have everything.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the free fitness! It is huge and you can participate in fitness classes etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel, travel, travel if you have the capacity! The east coast is interesting because the states are so different. Otherwise join the frat parties or invite people to go to the cinemax, get something to eat, grab a beer at Mitchs Tavern on Hillsborough Street or play some volleyball on campus!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy, but it was a culture shock. You could not get far without a car,  and I really missed cooking. However, the Americans are nice and welcoming!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Engage in a club, go on dates if you are single, ask to get a lift, ask for help on homeworks, get an American roomie and ask if they wanna hang out.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found it very hard to not be able to come around easily. The Americans do love their cars and I understand why, because they are their only form of transportation and the whole infrastructure is made for driving.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are so welcoming and kind towards you.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Figure out what you want to achieve with the exchange 
2. Put on your yes-hat because you only have a limited number of opportunities to experience this
3. Enjoy it and do not stress about school

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not be afraid to reach out for help, and try your best in engaging with locals and the other exchange students. Go to the sports events including the tailgates! It is crazy and fun! Also you have to go to the State Fair (A food festival with the weirdest food) It was an experience.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
To travel on the east coast! I am so happy that I got to experience so many states. I would recommend you to go to:
- Charleston, SC because of its history and how it looks like today 
- Blue Ridge Mountains in mid-october because of its beautifull colors and the black bears walking around!
- Boston, MA because of its architecture and good food
- New York, NY if you have not been there
- Washington D.C. if you are into history

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To not have a car.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
